steps.text: Combine heavy whipping cream, wine, flour, parsley, and salt in a medium saucepan over medium-high heat; bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low and simmer until thickened.

raw_recipe.headline: Creamy White Wine Sauce
raw_recipe.description: This white wine sauce is a luxuriously rich and creamy blend of heavy cream and wine flavored with parsley that pairs well with seafood and pasta.
raw_recipe.name: Creamy White Wine Sauce

recipeInstructions.text: Combine heavy whipping cream, wine, flour, parsley, and salt in a medium saucepan over medium-high heat; bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low and simmer until thickened.

review.reviewBody: We were having pasta one night, and I was trying to figure out something to go with it, saw that we had all the ingredients for this sauce and whipped it up in no time. It's now a family favorite and we make it all the time! It's really easy and sooooo good with pasta, chicken, fish, nearly anything!

This is a very basic white wine sauce that has potential to be amazing! When I made this, I added some 1/4 tsp garlic salt (in place of normal salt), 1 TBS garlic powder, and freshly chopped garlic as well. I also added a little flour to thicken. I let the heavy cream, wine and previous ingredients heat up. Then I added some sun dried tomatoes and peas. At the same time, I diced some chicken, seasoned it with salt and garlic powder and browned it in a different pan, then added a splash of white wine for added flavor. Once the chicken was almost cooked I added it to the sauce to finish cooking. I also added some spiral noodles and tossed it together. It came out delicious! This is a basic recipe but with some of your own touches it can be great!

Great wine sauce, i sauteed garlic in butter & then added the remaining ingredients. also added black pepper & half of freshly squeezed lemon to sauce while cooking. Cooked chicken in a cast iron pan with olive oil & butter until lightly browned, keep chicken warm in a 200 degrees oven. Put the sauce on the side so that everyone could put the sauce they wanted on the delicious dish it is a keeper. Served with Broccoli & Mashed Potato. Goes well with 14 hands cabernet wine.

I had high hopes but someone else pointed out that it was very salty and I have to agree. It was also too much flour because it thickened up quickly before the alcohol from the wine even cooked off. I wound up trying to fix it with some chicken broth, a spritz of lemon juice and topped with shredded Asiago, dumped over rice and broccoli, it wasn’t as salty.

I have never made a white wine sauce before and I decided to try this recipe. Everyone in my family really liked it. It turned out very well. I had read the other reviews and decided to cut the salt in half I also decided to reduce the wine before making the sauce and I added garlic.

Loved this sauce. I added 4 garlic cloves minced, and about 1/2 cup chicken broth. I added flour to get my desired consistency. I also added mushrooms to chicken medallions coated with Italian bread crumbs, and stirred everything together with pasta.

Simple, delicious sauce. Made it for the first time. The sauce did break, but I found a fix.. whisk an egg yolk with a little of the wine... then very slowly, while whisking, add your broken sauce. It completely fixed it.. it was smooth, and tasted great! Yes, when I was done eating I realized I just ate a whole stick of butter, but who cares if I get fat. My mother will still love me.

Good basic recipse, but I have to agree with those that commented on too much salt. Being warned beforehand, I cut the salt down by half and it was still too much for our taste (and we generally don't mind things a little salty). I added some half and half and a dash of sugar to counteract it. The sugar hint is one I learned from my mother - it "calms down" saltiness if you overdo it. Just a a little bit at a time though (by taste) so the sauce doesn't become noticeably sweet. After these corrections it was very good over my seared scallops and linguine pasta! Oh, I also added a clove of garlic, minced - sauteed in the pan in olive oil before adding the other ingredients.

This recipe was excellent, simple, and quick. I followed it exact, except for the fact that I doubled it. I made bowtie pasta, sauted some minced garlic, chopped onions and red bell pepper, mushrooms, peas, and threw in some leftover rotisserie chichen. After the pasta was drained I threw everything in the large pot and mixed it. (This was not salty, let alone too salty. Perhaps the other reviewer accidentally used a tablespoon of salt instead of a teaspoon).

This is how I made it, and I liked it:

- half an onion
- tsp minced garlic
- 1 cup half and half creamo (less fat)
- 3/4 cup wine
- 1 Tbsp flour
- tsp paprika
- seasoning salt until your desired saltiness
- cut up fresh basil

Fry onion & garlic in a pan until the onion is soft. Add the rest of the ingredients. Was very good.

When I first tried making this, I followed the recipe as is, and thought it was good, but not great. When I made it enough and finally got comfortable with it, I started to add some other ingredients to it. I first caramelized some garlic in a couple tablespoons of butter and a drizzle of olive oil. Then I added the wine and the heavy cream and let the wine reduce. I also added a little bit of chicken stock, and some dried herbs, and thought that it came out wonderfully with the additions. Very simple yet delectable sauce. Will be making this again. I love wine sauce.
I thought it was great. It was good how it was, but I did add 4 tablespoons of butter perfect for anything on top of asparagus, steak even eggs. It was quite wonderful.

I made this tonight and we loved it. Less one star because I might have added too much salt on the Halibut I was cooking, but I also added 2 tablespoons of butter which made it a bit creamier. Great recipe though!!

BUT....I omitted the salt, used half n half instead of heavy whipping cream, added some fresh herbs, garlic, butter, bone broth, & used cornstarch instead of flour to thicken. DELICIOUS!!!! You can switch this sauce up by using different herbs & also adding freshly grated parm or asiago!

I didn’t use as much salt BECAUSE I put cilantro and anchovies in the sauce, hit it with the boat motor and wow. Goes good on fish or chicken….. breakfast cereal…. Just joking on the cereal …anchovies are in Ceasers salad dressing also

Holy salt! OMG don't do it! I kinda thought it was too much salt, so I reduced it a tad...still WAYYYYY too salty..I quickly doubled up on the cream, flour and parsley....didn't seem to need any more wine..and it was STILL too salty... lesson learned....if I ever make it again I will salt my plate if needed!!!
Followed the recipe exactly. Came out Great! First time I've tried it, will definitely make again. Not too salty, not too much wine flavor. Family loved it.

Great recipe, Very simple to make and Delicious! 
Starr D

I found the same recipe years ago and loved it and can't believe it's been years since I made it again. I followed the recipe and don't have any complaints. I feel this is best used to add a layer of flavorful and not as the main focus of the dish. I love it over baked chicken cordon bleu. I've also used it on cheese and chicken ravioli. It's fairly potent so use it sparingly at first. If you want more you can always add more.
Too much wine! Not flavorful at all.
